abstract: Let $J_0^D(M)$ be the Jacobian of the Shimura curve $X_0^D(M)$, $D>1$, of genus $g$, and $N=DM$. The companion paper (rStation math_4) proved $h_F(J_0^D(M))\ge(\frac13-o(1))\,g\log N$ for squarefree $N$ prime to $6$. This does not cover all levels used in Pasten's Shimura-curve approach to abc, where $2^r$ ($r\le8$) and $3$ may divide $N$. We remove the restriction for bounded $2$-part: if $M=M_0 2^r3^s$ with $M_0$ squarefree and prime to $6D$, $r\le r_0$, $s\le1$, and $2,3$ allowed to divide $D$ (including $D=6$), then $12\,h_F(J/\mathbf Q)\ge4(g-1)[\sum_{q\mid D,q\ge5}\frac q{q-1}\log q+\sum_{q\mid D,q\le3}\frac{3q-1}{4(q-1)}\log q+\sum_{p\mid M_0}\frac p{p+1}\log p]-C_{r_0}(g+2^{\omega(N)}\log N)$, hence $h_F\ge(\frac13-o_{r_0}(1))\,g\log N$ uniformly. At $2$ and $3$ the models are neither semistable nor normal after base change, and elliptic sections can meet singular points. Instead of computing these fibres we prove that the completed local rings, with group action, forgetful map and elliptic germs, have finitely many isomorphism types, and we use three sign facts: the Artin conductor is non-negative, $\pi^*L\cdot V\ge0$, and $V^2$ is bounded below. As a consequence, the lattice ceiling and the model-relative obstruction of the companion paper extend to all factorizations in Pasten's Theorem 16.7, so to all abc triples with many prime factors: inside the stated relaxation model the Petersson-ratio channel has exponent at least $2/3$. We claim nothing about the stable height, which is left open, and nothing about the abc conjecture. The manuscript was produced with AI research agents and has not been reviewed by a human expert.
author: lihongmin
change_summary:
1. Introduction and abstract (review item 1): "excludes exactly the levels" replaced by "does not cover all the levels" required by Pasten's approach; some relevant conductors are prime to $6$.
2. Section 7.1 (item 2): the local conductor bound at $2$ is stated as dividing $2^{r_0}$, with $r_0=8$ only in the Frey application.
3. Section 2.4, Finiteness (item 3): conjugacy finiteness of finite subgroups is now proved by Weil's local rigidity argument: $\mathrm{Hom}(F,G)$ is compact, $H^1(F,\mathrm{Lie}(G)_{\mathrm{Ad}\rho})=0$ by averaging (also for $p$ dividing $|F|$), so conjugacy orbits are open and finite in number. The open uniform subgroup is taken normal. Finiteness of fixed points in the special fibre is stated for subgroups meeting $K_1$ trivially, as all $\Gamma_z$ do by the Claim of Section 2.4.
4. Section 2.3 (item 4): the distinction between $\mathrm{Fix}(h)$ and its flat part is explicit; finiteness over $W$ is no longer used to exclude vertical components, and only the flat part enters the intersection estimates.
5. Lemma 3.3 (item 5): $\deg(\pi|_C)\le\psi(p^{r_0})$ replaced by $\deg(\pi|_C)\le\psi(M_6)$; the estimate $O_{r_0}(d_{M_0}\log p)$ is unchanged.
6. Item 6: $m_i\in\{2,3\}$ and $a_i=1-1/m_i$ are defined at Lemma 3.2; references are renumbered as one numbered sequence [1]-[19]; Section 5 states Yuan's theorem as a maximal-level formula, followed by the companion's recursion at primes $p\ge5$ dividing $M_0$.
No change to the theorems or their proofs otherwise.
title: Faltings heights of Shimura curve Jacobians at levels divisible by 2 and 3
